Liuyang Cheng
liuyang5@illinois.edu
Research Profile

Ph.D. candidate in Mechanical Science and Engineering, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (expected Dec. 2026). Four peer-reviewed journal articles (including PNAS) and a first-author manuscript accepted by PNAS, spanning theory, manufacturing, and characterization of soft actuators.
Research Interests
Soft robotics; Bioinspired mechanism; Material actuator; Nonlinear mechanics of J-curve materials; Scalable actuator manufacturing and characterization.

Research Projects
Scalable Supercoiled Artificial Muscle Manufacturing
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign	June 2023 - On-going
Originated a continuous fabrication method and built an Arduino-based machine for scalable production
Developed theory linking stepper-motor speeds to twist density, geometry, and actuation performance
Octopus-Inspired Soft Robotic Arm
Mini-MURI Project, UIUC (ONR-funded)	Jan. 2023 - On-going
Advisors: Sameh H. Tawfick, Mattia Gazzola, James Pikul
Designed the tapered spiral geometry and built 2D prototypes with longitudinal and oblique muscles, demonstrating curling and twisting
Established theory relating arm geometry to the required muscle stroke
Added a mesh structure for greater flexibility; building a 3D spiral version
Actuator Characterization and Selection for Soft Robotic Design
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign	July 2024 - Oct. 2025
Developed a two-tensile-test method for actuator selection, validated on McKibben actuators
Smart Granular Robot with Vibration Sensing
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign	June 2023 – Mar. 2025
Advisors: Sameh H. Tawfick, Ahmed Elbanna
Developed a granular robot with vibration sensing, an on-board micro-motor, and inter-robot communication
Built a Python interface for group control; evaluated environmental interaction as a smart soil
Principles of Use of Tensile J-Curve Materials in Antagonistic Arrangements
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign	May 2022 - April 2025
Led the design of artificial ligaments reproducing the J-shaped tensile response of biological ligaments; identified the mechanisms of their nonlinearity and hysteresis
Originated principles of use of J-curve materials in linear and rotary antagonistic mechanisms (first-author manuscript accepted by PNAS)
Developed self-sensing ligaments using CNT surface coatings
Supercoiled & Hypercoiled Artificial Muscles
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign	Feb. 2022 - May 2024
Led the design of supercoiled and hypercoiled artificial muscles with embedded nichrome wires for uniform Joule heating; built an Arduino-based fabrication machine
Helped standardize isobaric and isometric testing methods
Insect-Scale Jumping Robot with Coiled Artificial Muscle
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign	June 2020 - May 2022
Fabricated coiled muscles and tested the insect-scale jumping robot (PNAS, 2023)
High Power Density, Large-Stroke Coiled Artificial Muscle System
Undergraduate Research Assistant, UIUC	Jan. 2020 - Aug. 2020
Optimized twisting and mandrel-coiling procedures across five approaches; quantified effects of material, diameter, and pre-stretch
Standardized fabrication and produced custom muscles for a collaborating group at Harvard

Technical Skills

Fabrication: twisted and coiled polymer actuators (mono-, super- and hyper-coiled), McKibben actuators, embedded nichrome Joule-heating, SIS fiber spinning, mandrel coiling, scalable muscle manufacturing
Characterization: isobaric and isometric actuator testing, tensile and cyclic testing, two-tensile-test actuator selection, J-curve nonlinearity and hysteresis analysis
Design and computation: CAD modeling, Arduino-based machine design and stepper-motor control, soft arm and mesh assembly, MATLAB, Python, machine learning
